ASIX 220.title: Indigeneities in Asia and Asian Diaspora
ASIX 220.description: Introduction to Indigenous methodologies, contemporary cultures, and issues of Indigenous peoples in Asia and Asian diaspora, and Indigenous-Asia relation-making in Canada.

ASIX 300.title: Topics in Asian Studies Crossings
ASIX 300.description: Transnational, transcultural, or transregional approaches to Asian and/or diasporic Asian literature, history, visual culture, religion, or communities. Topics vary from section to section. Consult Department for current offerings.

ASIX 315.title: Hong Kong Diaspora in Canada
ASIX 315.description: Various social issues relating to Hong Kong diaspora in Canada, particularly pertaining to their long history of migration to Canada; their cultural developments and experiences; and their challenges and contributions in their new cultural environment.

ASIX 320.title: Global Hong Kong
ASIX 320.description: A transdisciplinary exploration of the global connections of Hong Kong through the lens of cultural texts, social phenomena, and historical events.

ASIX 340.title: Orientalism in Popular Culture
ASIX 340.description: Exploration of Edward Said's Orientalism as a decolonial tool for analyzing popular culture across Asia.

ASIX 342.title: Cinematic Monsters of Asia
ASIX 342.description: Interrogates various tropes of monsters across modern Asian popular culture. Core theoretical concepts and approaches to understanding cultural and psychological fascination and anxiety regarding the monstrous.

ASIX 383.title: What is Modern Arabic?
ASIX 383.description: Examines Arabic language and writing using approaches from sociolinguistics, with examples from Arabic-speaking communities in the Arab world, the diasporas, and beyond. Basic Arabic language proficiency is strongly recommended through completion of ARBM 101, ARBC 101, or a placement interview.

ASIX 430.title: Indigenous Environmentalism in Asia
ASIX 430.description: Approaches to human-environment relationships through the works of Indigenous scholars from different parts of Asia. Restricted to students with third-year standing and above.

ASIX 440.title: Decolonizing Methodologies for Asian Studies
ASIX 440.description: Application and expansion of Critical Indigenous Studies methods, practices, and ethical principles for engaging Asian studies. Restricted to students with third-year standing and above.

ASIX 467.title: Islamic and Persianate Sufism
ASIX 467.description: Explore diverse and experiential interpretations of Islam through Sufi literature, art, music, and rituals. Restricted to students with second-year standing and above.
